title: Post-incident followup: hosted GPU 'thundering prefill' regression, queue amplification and safety-net hardening
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: During the 2026-02-26 capacity incident the hosted GPU pool experienced a rapid queue amplification caused by a prefill/prefetch regression in our autoscaler and prewarm logic. Symptoms were long tail latencies, tenant-request queuing, and aggressive throttling that cascaded into churned autoscale attempts and slower recovery. This ticket tracks concrete follow-ups from the postmortem: root cause fixes, telemetry/enrichment, temporary safety-nets, and medium-term improvements to avoid regression recurrence.

Root cause (short): A change in prefill timing (commit abc12345) removed jitter and extended simultaneous prefill attempts when multiple tenant slots were priming. Combined with missing tenant-level queue length histograms and our admission controller not applying exponential backoff, this produced a thundering prefill effect and queue buildup that saturated GPU pools. Autoscaler oscillations then caused repeated drain/recreate cycles and longer outage window.

Key evidence and artifacts:
- Incident timeline and metrics: https://dash.redwoodinfra/incident/2026-02-26-gpu-exhaustion
- Postmortem doc: https://confluence.redwood/inference/postmortems/2026-02-gpu-prefill
- Related PR where regression introduced: github.com/redwood/inference/commit/abc12345
- Hotfix PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/12456 (reintroduce jitter + backoff)

Decisions made in the postmortem meeting:
- Immediate revert of the deterministic prefill path and ship short-term hotfix (done, see PR #12456).
- Add tenant-level queue-length and prefill-attempt metrics before wider rollout.
- Implement admission-controller exponential backoff and a hard safety cap per-tenant during priming.
- Enhance autoscaler hysteresis with a minimum cooldown window after pool priming to avoid oscillation.

Action items (owner — ETA — status):
1) Fix: Reintroduce jittered prefill and per-tenant prefill token bucket. Owner: Marcus Patel — ETA: 2026-03-05 — status: Done (merged GH#12456).
2) Metric: Add tenant queue-length histogram, prefill_attempts counter, and prefill_duration summary to hosted telemetry. Owner: Priya Singh — ETA: 2026-03-12 — status: In Progress.
3) Admission: Exponential backoff in admission controller + hard per-tenant priming cap (configurable). Owner: Diego Alvarez — ETA: 2026-03-19 — status: In Progress.
4) Autoscaler: Hysteresis/cooldown rule to prevent immediate scale-down after a priming spike. Owner: Leah Brooks — ETA: 2026-03-26 — status: Planned.
5) Runbook: Update hosted GPU drain/runbook with new triage steps and automated mitigations (prefill-revert, throttle toggle). Owner: Marcus Patel — ETA: 2026-03-08 — status: In Progress.
6) Testing: Add synthetic stress tests reproducing simultaneous tenant prefill under different jitter settings and sequence length distributions. Owner: SRE Team (owner: Omar Rivera) — ETA: 2026-03-22 — status: Planned.
7) Alerts: Add a short-latency alert for prefill_attempts > threshold and tenant_queue_length P99 increase. Owner: Observability (owner: Priya Singh) — ETA: 2026-03-12 — status: In Progress.

Telemetry and observability gaps to close:
- No tenant-level queue length histograms existed prior to the incident; add histograms and per-tenant tagging.
- Prefill attempts were only logged at pool-level; instrument individual prefill start/finish with runtime correlation IDs.
- Need synthetic canary and chaos tests in CI that exercise multi-tenant priming at scale.

Temporary mitigations already applied:
- Hotfix revert with jitter reintroduced (GH#12456) rolled to 50% then 100% across hosted pools.
- Emergency throttle flag added to console to limit concurrent prefill attempts per-tenant (console toggle: hosted.prefill.limit).
- Manual pool priming cooldown enforced for 30m after any large autoscale event until hysteresis shipped.

Longer-term proposals (post-ship work):
- Model-aware priming: use sequence-length distribution and model KV cache size to size prefill work more conservatively per-tenant.
- Admission scoring: incorporate tenant historical prefill error-rate and recent queue growth into admission priority.
- Autoscaler meta-heuristics: keep a short memory window to detect priming-induced spikes and avoid reactive scale-down.

Risks and trade-offs discussed:
- More conservative prefill reduces tail latency but increases cold-start exposure for small tenants; we'll mitigate by targeted caching and tenant-specified warm targets.
- Adding per-tenant telemetry increases cardinality and cost; team will add sampling (1% detailed traces + aggregated histograms) to balance cost.

Follow-ups/Dependencies:
- Dependency: Observability changes must land before full rollout of the admission backoff (see dependency ENG-273821).
- Dependency: Chaos tests on perf infra to validate hysteresis behavior (SRE schedule required).

Comments and timeline of updates: See comments array for running record.
